paras: The whitecap notices to Black residents of Robertson County, Texas, were printed warnings, reported in an Austin dispatch of October 30, 1903, ordering the county's Black population to leave under threat of being "whitecapped." According to the dispatch, the Black residents were alarmed and many were leaving. The known coverage consists of one brief wire item reprinted by newspapers in North Dakota, South Dakota and Minnesota.

Robertson County lay north of Austin, according to the dispatch, which said that "the negroes of Robertson county" had been warned by whitecaps "to leave the country under threats of being whitecapped." The warnings took the form of printed notices tacked on trees "throughout the country districts." The dispatch did not name any town, any of the whitecaps or any of the people warned, and it did not give the date the notices went up. It reported that the Black residents were "much alarmed" and that "many of them are leaving."
No report of arrests, an investigation or any official response appears in the coverage, and no later account of how many people left was found.

The story reached print as a single four-sentence Austin dispatch under the headline "WHITECAPS GIVE WARNING. Negroes of Robertson County, Tex., Ordered to Leave." On October 30 it ran on the front pages of the Bismarck Daily Tribune, the Bemidji Daily Pioneer and the Madison Daily Leader, followed by the Morris Tribune of Minnesota on October 31 and the Jamestown Weekly Alert on November 5. Each paper printed the text unchanged and without comment, and the Jamestown paper set it above its local market prices. No Texas paper's account and no coverage in the Black press were found.
